newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas confident of higher 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Adidas confident of higher 1997 profit.

text.p: German sportswear maker Adidas AG said Wednesday it was confident it would report higher sales and profit for 1997 after record results in 1996 and would meet market expectations.

"All in all, we are confident that our business prospects for the full year are very favourable for ensuring further steady growth in sales and profitability, and thus living up to the expectations of our investors and the financial community," Adidas Chief Executive Robert Louis-Dreyfus said in the text of a speech at the company's annual general meeting.
Louis-Dreyfus said Adidas' order backlog at the end of March was indicative of the company's strength, which had risen 36 percent during the 1997 first quarter compared with the same period in 1996.

Adidas, best known for its three-stripe logo, reported a 43 percent rise in first-quarter net sales to 1.7 billion marks ($998.4 million), while pretax profit rose 42 percent to 243 million marks ($142.8 million).

Net sales for 1996 rose 35 percent to 4.7 billion marks ($2.8 billion), while pretax profit rose 50 percent to 444 million marks ($260.9 million) behind a 51 percent surge in apparel sales and a 21 percent gain in footwear sales.

The positive outlook for 1997 underpinned Adidas stock in market trade, reaching a new record high at 191.50 marks ($112.5 million) before easing to trade up 1.50 marks (88 cents) to 191 marks ($112.22).
